result.summary: I added command support for JMAK, over TCP and over SMS. The new class `org.traccar.protocol.JmakProtocolEncoder(Protocol, boolean textChannel)` builds TCP commands as `$<id>;<value>;|...#` and SMS commands as `JMAK#<s|e>;<id>;<value>#...#`. Over SMS, reboot is the literal `JMAK#REBOOT#`. `JmakProtocol` now lists the same 12 command types for data and for text commands. It sets the SMS encoder with `setTextCommandEncoder`, and the TCP pipeline now has a `StringEncoder` plus the encoder. The new `JmakProtocolEncoderTest` checks every command on both channels, including the examples from the task. `make check-fast` passes: Checkstyle is clean and 613 tests ran with 0 failures. I did not run `make check` (the full Gradle build). In the task text, the TCP prefix was garbled, so I used `$`, which is what the examples show. There is no "movement" command type in Traccar, so the movement alarm uses `Command.TYPE_ALARM_VIBRATION`.

changes.summary: New encoder: one parameter builder for both TCP and SMS formats. Covers custom, engine stop/resume, output control (index 1/2/3 -> 34/94/167), periodic positions (2), set odometer (30), set connection (13 for an IPv4 server, 43 for a domain, then 12), reboot (93=1 over TCP, JMAK#REBOOT# over SMS), set speed limit (e16=1 then s17), low battery (e57), power removal (e55) and movement (e59).
Lists the supported data and text commands, sets the SMS text command encoder, and adds StringEncoder and JmakProtocolEncoder to the TCP pipeline.
New tests for every command over TCP and SMS, plus one encode through a channel.
Log entry for this change, as AGENTS.md asks.

human_needed.question: Should the JMAK movement alarm (parameter 59) use Command.TYPE_ALARM_VIBRATION, or should a new command type be added?
human_needed.why: Traccar has no movement alarm command type. I used alarmVibration because it is the closest existing type.

human_needed.question: Is the TCP command prefix '$'?
human_needed.why: In the task text, the TCP prefix was garbled. I took '$' from the examples ($34;1;#).

human_needed.question: For set connection, should IPv6 addresses also use parameter 13?
human_needed.why: Only dotted IPv4 addresses select parameter 13. Any other server value uses parameter 43 (domain name).

harness_gaps.problem: It says nothing about SMS (text) command encoders (setTextCommandEncoder and setSupportedTextCommands), how to test an encoder (verifyEncode, or calling encodeCommand directly), or the StringEncoder needed in the pipeline for text encoders. I found these by reading other protocols.

No list that maps the Command.TYPE_* constants to their usual KEY_* attributes, for example that setSpeedLimit and setOdometer use KEY_DATA and outputControl uses KEY_INDEX and KEY_DATA. I had to grep other encoders to find these.
